title: G3 Candidate Enumerator
objective: Make exact genus-3 Weil-candidate enumeration fast while preserving exact Sturm semantics and ordinary Python fallback

handoff.summary: Replaced general rational Sturm allocation on the hot path with an exactly equivalent cubic endpoint/derivative criterion, retained the old Sturm implementation as a differential oracle, and added a source-transparent packed exact candidate scanner. Unfiltered enumeration uses the compiled scanner only after input validation and respects both public resource limits; filtered completion keeps its bounded dynamic stream. Dense CPython and compiled Sage.js tests cover arbitrary coefficients, residue scans, endpoint/repeated roots, resource limits, and GMP promotion. The exact source compiled and returned identical small and promoted-integer streams on Linux x64/arm64, macOS arm64, and native Windows x64. The native benchmark is 102x-303x faster than the old Sturm scan at p=101..10007 and completes the p=1000003 residue class in about 0.20 seconds on the development x64 host.
risks: The coordinator stopped a duplicate lane-wide pnpm test:native rebuild after integration had already passed production registration; scoped architecture, strict, public completion, dense differential, and four-platform compiled-kernel checks are green.
Tests and the benchmark live beside the claimed implementation because the hyperelliptic lane cannot claim repository-wide test/bench paths; integration may relocate them.
Packed IntegerBuffer materialization dominates the largest tested row, so a future streaming certificate interface may outperform exhaustive candidate materialization.
next_steps: Move or wrap the in-package differential and benchmark drivers in the central test and benchmark manifests.
